links.outcome: Discrimination versus calibration metrics after class-imbalance resampling
links.effect: ROC-AUC change -0.002 to -0.01; Brier scores increased 0.029-0.080 with marked calibration intercept and slope deviations, so rank-based metrics alone hid distorted predicted risks.
links.quote: The consistent dissociation between discrimination and calibration highlights that rank-based metrics alone are insufficient for evaluating clinical utility.

unlisted_practices: Avoiding 1:1 class-imbalance resampling (SMOTE, random undersampling, random oversampling) when training clinical risk models; using threshold adjustment instead to preserve calibration
